nodes.label: Coding Behavior Contract (13 Rules)
nodes.rationale: Core operating rules for any Claude session/subagent working in this repo: think before coding, simplicity first, surgical changes, goal-driven execution, no non-language work in the model, hard token budgets, surface conflicts, read before write, tests check behavior, checkpoint long operations, convention beats novelty, fail visibly, expand mental model rather than redirect action.

nodes.label: Eventar → CPD Platform Pivot (2026-07-03)
nodes.rationale: Eventar pivoted from an internal workshop manager to a CPD/CME/CE event + credit platform for regulated professions, HK launch with HKCP as first accrediting body. Backend-first roadmap; frontend frozen until Milestone-M2 review.

nodes.label: Audit insert last (pivot-era hard rule)
nodes.rationale: Any transaction writing audit_events emits the audit event as the LAST statement before commit; the chain trigger holds pg_advisory_xact_lock until commit — prevents ordering/race issues in the audit hash chain.

nodes.label: Measurement vs inference (automation rule)
nodes.rationale: Automation acts only on deterministic measurements (rate limits, Turnstile, OTP failure counts); inference signals produce flags for humans, never automatic action. No IP-level enforcement on authenticated routes.

nodes.label: Multi-tenancy rule (organisation_id + RLS)
nodes.rationale: Every new domain table carries organisation_id + RLS; Q20 reversed the old single-org decision 6.3.

nodes.label: Frontend freeze rule
nodes.rationale: While frontend freeze holds: only backend, migrations, Server Actions, and tests are in scope; no new surfaces or restyles.

nodes.label: Hard rules (never break)
nodes.rationale: Staff identity keyed on email not auth.users.id; email_log inserted before send; requireStaff() at top of every staff Server Action (proxy.ts in Next 16, not middleware.ts); service-role key only in lib/supabase/admin.ts with server-only; RLS enabled on every table; single main branch; no premature external services; three-layer validation; three-layer auth; no PII in logs.

nodes.label: Pre-deploy gates — ALL CLOSED
nodes.rationale: Four pre-public-deploy gates resolved: PII enumeration oracle fixed on /checkin/confirm, CSPRNG registration codes via crypto.randomInt(), host-header spoofing fixed via lib/origin.ts, migration history drift reconciled 26/26.

nodes.label: Staff MFA workstream (deferred to Sprint 4)
nodes.rationale: Password+TOTP backend on auth.mfa, mfa_is_fresh helper, wrapper freshness-gate wiring, enrolment UI, TOTP-mandatory enforcement; moved wholesale from Sprint 2 because it had no Sprint 2 consumer; re-entry when signing ships.

nodes.label: pseudonymise_user privilege-escalation fix
nodes.rationale: Slice 0.3 DDL as drafted was SECURITY DEFINER + GRANT EXECUTE TO authenticated, letting any logged-in user erase anyone via PostgREST RPC. Fixed design inlines an eventar_staff + status='active' check inside the function, raises insufficient_privilege, and writes a user_pseudonymised audit event in the same transaction.

nodes.label: Audit hash chain race + ordering fix
nodes.rationale: As drafted, no advisory lock in the trigger and (created_at, uuid_v4) ordering was non-deterministic because identity nextval fires before BEFORE-triggers. Fixed design: chain_seq bigint identity column overridden by the trigger via nextval() after acquiring pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('audit_events_chain')); ordering by chain_seq only. Convention: audit insert is the last statement before commit.
nodes.norm_label: audit hash chain race + ordering fix

nodes.label: Lookup miss-rate signal (replaces RLS-deny-counter)
nodes.rationale: 'RLS deny counter' signal can never fire because RLS on SELECT filters silently. Replaced by lookup miss-rate: fraction of parameterised lookups per session returning empty/404; flag at >60% over 100 requests in 10 min.

nodes.label: Abuse-control design — measurement vs inference
nodes.rationale: Automation is safe when the trigger is a measurement; dangerous when it is an inference. Measurements can auto-act (rate limits, Turnstile, OTP failure bursts); inferences (behavioural signals — cadence, endpoint traversal, lookup miss-rate, endpoint diversity) produce flags only, forever.

nodes.label: Sprint 2 Finding 1 — audit enforcement must be a DB-function shape
nodes.rationale: Every PostgREST RPC executes as its own transaction; an application-layer wrapper calling write_audit_event after a mutation runs the audit write in a separate transaction, violating audit-insert-last. Audited mutations must be SECURITY DEFINER database functions ending with the audit write — pseudonymise_user is the canonical shape. write_audit_event EXECUTE grant revoked from authenticated.
nodes.norm_label: sprint 2 finding 1 — audit enforcement must be a db-function shape

nodes.label: Sprint 2 Finding 2 — Turnstile-deferral window residual risk
nodes.rationale: During the Turnstile deferral window, unauthenticated endpoints have flat per-IP rate limits only — no escalating block, no bot challenge, no strike ladder. A persistent attacker can hammer /login and /otp/* at just-under-rate-limit indefinitely. Acceptable only while the platform is not publicly exposed; public exposure gates on Turnstile provisioning.
nodes.norm_label: sprint 2 finding 2 — turnstile-deferral window residual risk

nodes.label: email_log insert-before-send idempotency pattern
nodes.rationale: Insert email_log row BEFORE sending via Resend. Reversed order risks duplicates if the process crashes between send and log; the 'miss one' failure mode is recoverable (manual re-send) while 'send twice' undermines trust — asymmetric cost drives the ordering choice.

nodes.label: Server-derived timezone rationale
nodes.rationale: Timezone is derived server-side from venue lat/lng via offline tz-lookup so it becomes derived state, not trusted user input; browser never sees or computes TZ, keeping the value tamper-proof and consistent.

nodes.label: Accordion-over-wizard navigation rationale
nodes.rationale: User wanted freedom to fill sections in any order; a wizard's strict gating would force a back-button cascade that complicates state. Accordion with per-section Done buttons (no auto-collapse on blur) gives the right level of structure without surprise behaviour.

nodes.label: Mapbox HK proximity-bias rationale
nodes.rationale: proximity (Victoria Harbour lng/lat) is the single highest-leverage knob to surface HK landmarks like HKCEC without restricting matches; no country filter preserves global fallback for non-HK addresses.

nodes.label: Nominatim-over-Mapbox decision rationale
nodes.rationale: Direct curl tests against five providers proved Mapbox has near-zero coverage of HK/Asian landmarks (HKCEC search returned a Vietnam result 1,679km away); Nominatim returned the correct HKCEC lat/lon on first query. Zero setup friction (no key/billing) fits current staff-only scale (~500 searches/month) against Nominatim's 1 req/sec public-instance budget.

nodes.label: C1 — publishEvent ignored RLS denials (silent failure)
nodes.rationale: .update().eq() returns 0 affected rows when an organizer tries to publish another organizer's event, but the action returned success and revalidated — pure silent failure. Fixed by chaining .select('id').maybeSingle() and throwing when data is null.
nodes.norm_label: c1 — publishevent ignored rls denials (silent failure)

nodes.label: C4 — proxy signOut() cookie/response-object mismatch
nodes.rationale: signOut() wrote clear-cookies to res, but the function returned a different NextResponse.redirect() object, so the browser stayed signed in and the next visit triggered an infinite redirect loop. Fixed via a redirectWithCookies() helper that copies res.cookies onto the redirect — same bug class as the /auth/callback fix.

nodes.label: Inline base64 QR storage decision
nodes.rationale: QR PNGs are returned as inline base64 data URLs rather than stored in a Supabase Storage bucket — avoids adding a storage surface for a small (~3-5KB), on-demand-regenerable artifact.

nodes.label: Idempotent UPDATE ... WHERE status != 'attended' race-safety pattern
nodes.rationale: markAttended and selfCheckIn both UPDATE ... WHERE registration_code = code AND status != 'attended', returning 0 rows on a race between staff-tablet and self-checkin or duplicate scans. Surfacing the 0-row case as a distinct 'already attended' error rather than reporting fake success follows the fail-visibly rule (CLAUDE.md rule 12).

nodes.label: Cross-event scan tolerance decision

nodes.label: Idempotent check-in pattern (WHERE status != 'attended')

nodes.label: Audit-insert-last, same-transaction rule
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md pivot-era hard rule: any transaction writing audit_events emits the audit event as the LAST statement before commit, since the chain trigger holds pg_advisory_xact_lock until commit — guarantees lock order == chain_seq order == chain order.

nodes.label: BASELINE-DELTAS §3.2 — chain_seq drawn inside advisory lock
nodes.rationale: Identity defaults evaluate at tuple formation before BEFORE triggers fire, so a pre-assigned chain_seq's order need not match lock-acquisition order; overwriting chain_seq inside the advisory lock guarantees correct ordering.

nodes.label: D1 — Restrict write_audit_event grant (revoke authenticated EXECUTE)
nodes.rationale: Closes the audit-authenticity gap from Sprint 1: a malicious authenticated user could forge a legitimately-chained row with false actor claims by calling write_audit_event directly via PostgREST. Every audited mutation instead becomes a SECURITY DEFINER fn ending in the audit write; the postgres-owned definer inherits audit_writer's EXECUTE, so legitimate paths are unaffected.
nodes.norm_label: d1 — restrict write_audit_event grant (revoke authenticated execute)

nodes.label: ADR Finding 1 — PostgREST RPCs run as separate transactions
nodes.rationale: An app-level wrapper calling write_audit_event after a mutation runs the audit write in a separate transaction, violating audit-insert-last-same-transaction; forces the SECURITY DEFINER gate→mutation→audit-write-LAST shape.
nodes.norm_label: adr finding 1 — postgrest rpcs run as separate transactions

nodes.label: P2 — Global audit-chain lock discipline
nodes.rationale: The audit chain serializes all writes through one global advisory lock held for transaction duration; audited definer functions must complete slow work before the audit-write and have no side effects between audit-write and commit.
